title: Philip Blevins v. Westminster Presbytery
disposition_detail: Complaint sustained on the sole issue that the Blevins/Seufert complaint was timely filed; the February 3, 2004 commission ruling and Presbytery's denial of Blevins's complaint were held erroneous. Remanded to Westminster Presbytery to rehear the Westminster Session and Warhurst complaints with the merits of the Blevins/Seufert complaint duly considered. The SJC did not decide the merits of the wife's divorce grounds or whether the Session erred in May 2003.
first_summary: SJC sustained TE Philip Blevins's complaint against Westminster Presbytery, holding the Blevins/Seufert complaint was timely and reversing the commission's untimeliness ruling. It reasoned that the wife's April 2003 letter was essentially a BCO 35-13 request based on new evidence (Presbytery's adultery ruling), and the Session's May 2003 denial was a new complaintable decision. The SJC remanded for Presbytery to rehear the matter and decide the wife's divorce grounds.
summary: SJC sustained TE Philip Blevins's complaint against Westminster Presbytery, holding the Blevins/Seufert complaint was timely despite the commission's February 3, 2004 untimeliness ruling. The wife's April 2003 letter was essentially a BCO 35-13 request to review new evidence, and the Session's May 2003 denial was a new complaintable decision. The SJC did not decide the wife's divorce grounds or the Session's merits; it remanded for Presbytery to rehear the Session and Warhurst complaints with the Blevins/Seufert merits considered. A concurrence added that no full new trial is required.
